scope: Original foundations for own Human Biology references 9.1–9.10. Source/logic and bounded browser review, not independent examiner calibration or chapter certification.
qualifications: Blood transports heat energy; heat is not a dissolved chemical. Urea is made in liver and transported toward kidneys.
Tissue-fluid exchange includes filtration and lymph drainage; no fixed immediate venous reabsorption percentage asserted.
Mature human red cells lack a nucleus. Biconcavity, haemoglobin and flexibility each linked to a function.
ABO surface antigens distinguished from plasma antibodies. Group O lacks A/B antigens, not every possible antigen.
Compatibility model explicitly limited to red cells and ABO; Rh, other groups and crossmatching not replaced by a classroom chart.
Phagocytosis distinguished from antigen-specific lymphocyte responses. Soluble fibrinogen and insoluble fibrin correctly ordered.
Vessels defined by direction relative to heart, including pulmonary oxygenation exceptions. Pulse identified as pressure wave.
Pulmonary/systemic, renal and hepatic portal routes checked. Ventricular wall demand linked to pressure; valves respond passively to pressure differences.
